newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Doctors found second tumour in Havel's lung - paper.
newsitem.headline: Doctors found second tumour in Havel's lung - paper.

text.p: Doctors removed two tumours from the right lung of Czech President Vaclav Havel in December, not just the single malignant tumour initially reported, the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes said on Saturday.
It is the first time doctors have publicly disclosed the presence of a second tumour, which they say was benign and did not affect the 60-year-old president's health.
"There was no reason to analyse the details," the paper quoted chief surgeon Pavel Pafko as saying in justification of the silence thus far.
Doctors said they learned of the second tumour only during the December 2 surgery, in which they removed half of the President's right lung, as it had not been uncovered by earlier X-rays.
Havel, a heavy smoker for decades, left hospital in late December after the operation and a subsequent battle with pneumonia forced doctors to temporarily place him on a respirator.

The former dissident playwright-turned-politician has said his life was "literally hanging by a thread" at one stage, prompting a public debate over whether Havel's care was adequate throughout the ordeal.
But his health has since improved rapidly, allowing him to re-marry on January 4, to 43-year-old Czech actress Dagmar Veskrnova. Havel's first wife Olga died of cancer last January at the age of 62.

The president has rejected repeated suggestions that smoking caused his illness, instead blaming bouts of pneumonia he suffered in jail under the former Communist regime, which he helped to peacefully overthrow in 1989.
But he also announced last week that he had given up smoking and drinking, "at least temporarily".
